chapter: Arrangers, Bill Robinson and Coleman Hawkins
title: Staying in Coleman Hawkins' mother's house in St. Joe
summary: As a school basketball player Thomas stayed in Hawkins' family house in St. Joseph and learned Hawkins started on cello.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: But the greatest thrill I had was when I made four tunes for Coleman Hawkins.

Yes. See, I knew Coleman personally, because I used to take... A lot of times when we had a contract for Coleman, I used to take the contracts up to his house to get him to sign, and he'd sign them, and I'd take them back to the office the next day. But I just idolized Coleman Hawkins, because man, to me he was the greatest tenor saxophonist that ever played! And I had the privilege of staying at his mother's house in St. Joe, Missouri.
He was just coming up. That's where I found out a lot about him.
Well, you didn't mention that when you said you were coming through St. Joe and all those towns when you were coming up.

I was playing basketball in school. And I was still playing saxophone. But see, I'd heard of Coleman Hawkins then, because Coleman Hawkins used to play with Mamie Smith. He used to go on the road with Mamie Smith. And they'd never come to Topeka, somehow or another. I knew

he was in the neighborhood. But when I was playing basketball, on the basketball team they used to farm us out like they did the bands, at people's houses. And I had the privilege of staying in Coleman Hawkins' house. And I knew of him. So I talked...
What was his mother like? Do you remember?

She was beautiful. And that's where I found out... You know, one of his first instruments... I don't know whether the first one was piano or not. But one of his first instruments was cello. And to me, I idolized him... That's why he played that tenor saxophone so well.
